name: Joan of Arc
hook: The peasant visionary who saved Orléans, crowned a king and was burned at Rouen.

facts.label: Siege of Orléans
facts.statement: Joan lifted the Siege of Orléans in May 1429, turning the tide of the Hundred Years' War against the English.

facts.label: Charles VII
facts.statement: Joan fought to restore the Dauphin, Charles VII, and stood by him at his coronation in Reims cathedral in July 1429.

facts.label: Rouen
facts.statement: Joan was burned at the stake in 1431 at the Place du Vieux-Marche in Rouen, on the Seine.

facts.label: the Seine
facts.statement: Joan's ashes were thrown into the Seine after her execution, according to tradition.

facts.label: Saint Joan
facts.statement: Joan was canonized in 1920; George Bernard Shaw's play Saint Joan opened in 1923.

facts.label: Personal Recollections of Joan of Arc
facts.statement: Mark Twain wrote Personal Recollections of Joan of Arc and called it, oddly, his favorite of his own works.

facts.label: Jhesus Maria banner
facts.statement: Joan carried a banner sprinkled with lilies and inscribed 'Jhesus Maria'; Shakespeare's Henry VI calls her a holy prophetess.
